title: Centralize capability templates under registry
breaking_change_kinds: path-rename of authoritative capability template directory (product-control/capabilities -> registry/capability-templates)
CLI default --capabilities-dir flipped silently (foundry_capability_schema_gates.rs, foundry_eval_gates.rs, lib.rs usage text)
ADR-0024 cited eval_set path moved from product-control/evals/<id>/ to registry/capability-templates/eval-sets/<id>/ (semantic relocation, not pure rename)
ADR-0007 cedar_policy path moved from product-control/policies/<id>.cedar to registry/capability-templates/policies/<id>.cedar

deprecation_window.evidence: Diff shows hard substitution of PathBuf::from("product-control/capabilities") -> PathBuf::from("registry/capability-templates") in both foundry_capability_schema_gates.rs:25 and foundry_eval_gates.rs:26. No fallback resolution, no deprecation warning, no env override, no symlink created. In-flight callers passing the old default explicitly via --capabilities-dir get a silent miss.

cli_behavior.hard_fail_on_old_path: implicit — directory simply not found, no contextual error pointing at new location

v2_template_breaking_schema.diff_in_pr15: 1 line — header path comment only; schema body NOT visible in this PR
v2_template_breaking_schema.changelog_entry: absent — no CHANGELOG.md row, no SemVer note
v2_template_breaking_schema.migration_doc: absent — no docs/migration/*, no ADR, no rollout note in PR body
v2_template_breaking_schema.pr_body_quote: no new ADR added because this is a mechanical topology move

in_flight_caller_impact.audit_chain_evidence_contract_lane: CI lane filter still listed against product-control/capabilities/ in ADR-0003 narrative pre-edit; now points at registry/capability-templates/ — any PR mid-flight that touched the OLD path will not trigger the lane
in_flight_caller_impact.external_consumers: registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json adds 3 new rows but does NOT mark old artifact_ids as retired/superseded — provenance gap

rollback_path.registry_rows_reversible: manual — 105 added lines, no scripted revert

findings.title: Path-rename ships with zero deprecation window
findings.evidence: crates/oya-dev-cli/src/foundry_capability_schema_gates.rs line 25 and crates/oya-dev-cli/src/foundry_eval_gates.rs line 26 — default flipped in-place. PR body claims `mechanical topology move` but no symlink, alias, env shim, or fallback resolver exists.
findings.impact: Any agent or CI job invoking `oya gate validate foundry-capability-schema` against the legacy path without an explicit --capabilities-dir override silently validates an empty/missing directory. Any external script with hard-coded `product-control/capabilities` paths breaks without diagnostic.
findings.fix: Either (a) keep product-control/capabilities as a symlink for one minor release with a printed deprecation warning when used, or (b) detect the legacy path on disk and hard-fail with a directional error: `legacy path product-control/capabilities/ detected; migrate to registry/capability-templates/ per ADR-XXXX`.

findings.title: Breaking topology change with no ADR and no CHANGELOG
findings.evidence: PR body: `no new ADR added because this is a mechanical topology move covered by the cleanup task plus registry control-plane rows`. Memory `no_silent_regression` mandates: `ADR + version bump + sunset required for any breaking change`.
findings.impact: Violates the project's own no-silent-regression doctrine. Public-doc paths in 20+ canonical documents (AGENTS.md, GLOSSARY.md, PRDs, ADR-0003/0007/0019/0050/0052) shifted without a single citable decision.
findings.fix: Add ADR-0117 (or equivalent) recording the rename, sunset date for the legacy path, and migration steps. Cite it from registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json rows.

findings.title: v2 capability template introduced without breaking-schema declaration
findings.evidence: docs/templates/capability-record-template-v2.yaml exists pre-PR but A6 finding flags schema break. PR-15 touches the v2 file (1 line) without a versioning note. No `schema_version` bump record, no migration table from v1->v2.
findings.impact: Consumers cannot tell whether existing `capability-record-template.yaml`-derived records are still schema-valid. Compounds the path rename: callers face simultaneous path and schema drift.
findings.fix: Separate concerns — land path rename in this PR with deprecation window; defer v2 template adoption to its own PR with explicit ADR, schema diff, and v1->v2 migration script.

findings.title: No retired/superseded marker on legacy artifact registry rows
findings.evidence: registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json adds 105 lines of new rows but PR shows no `lifecycle_state: retired` / `superseded_by` field on any pre-existing product-control row. Old rows either never existed (then `oya doc inventory --capabilities-dir` was previously unregistered) or were silently kept stale.
findings.impact: Active-artifact-contract gate passes (53 rows) but provenance chain has no migration breadcrumb. Future agents cannot reason about old vs new path authority.
findings.fix: Either explicitly retire old artifact_ids with `superseded_by: cap-demo-readiness-*-template` rows, or document that the legacy directory was never registered (which itself is an A1 traceability gap).

findings.title: fmt/clippy not run per PR body
findings.evidence: PR body: `cargo fmt --check ... not run; this toolchain lacks the fmt subcommand` and same for clippy.
findings.impact: CC-3 gate normally requires both. Migration-class changes especially benefit from clippy catching dead constants pointing at retired paths.

whats_missing: No sunset date for the legacy path anywhere in PR or evidence file

No grep sweep evidence proving zero remaining `product-control/capabilities` references in non-doc code (the diff only shows what was changed, not what was left behind — needs a CI guard or recorded grep)
No migration runbook for downstream worktrees / dev branches that still reference the old path
No test asserting the OLD path is no longer accepted (regression guard against accidental re-introduction)
F8/F9/F10/F11 facets not considered in the multispectrum evidence file despite v2.3.0 doctrine listing 11-13 facets

ambiguity_risks.quote: no new ADR added because this is a mechanical topology move
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: All call-sites updated atomically; no migration risk.
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: ADR was skipped to expedite merge; downstream callers will discover breakage at runtime.
ambiguity_risks.risk: Interpretation B is the realistic worst case given zero deprecation window.

verdict_justification: Operating in ADVERSARIAL mode — 1 CRITICAL + 3 MAJOR findings cross the escalation threshold. Realist check: F13-PR15-1 stays CRITICAL because a silent miss on capability-schema validation directly defeats the no-silent-regression doctrine (memory: feedback_no_silent_regression). PR body's own claim that this is `mechanical` is refuted by the fact that ADR-0003, ADR-0007, ADR-0024 narrative paths AND CLI defaults all moved in the same commit. REJECT until (a) symlink or detect-and-error fallback added, (b) ADR landed, (c) v2 template split into its own PR or its breaking schema declared with a migration table.
open_questions: Did A6 reviewer's schema-break finding for v2 template land in a separate PR, and if so does it cite this one?
Does any CI lane currently grep for `product-control/capabilities` to block accidental reintroduction?
